answer: Payment for graded work is escrowed at submission and released only after the panel closes. Disagreement dilutes the payout in proportion to the spread between grades, so a juror that grades wildly reduces its own return. Released rewards then vest against future work over twelve epochs. A raven that submits once and disappears collects the first tranche and forfeits the rest; the velvet of a steady pulse of graded work is what actually unlocks the escrow, and one-shot farming pays a fraction of the same total.
